method: Original exercises read first; all 11 independently solved before reading any D656 author lesson, task, answer or native-pass file. Local arithmetic only. Figure 43 inventory and hash reuse is specifically authorized.

approved_figure_reuse.inventory: One unbranched series RLC path: one rectangular resistor R, one two-plate capacitor C, one four-lobed coil L, two source terminals. No current arrow or polarity sign.
approved_figure_reuse.approval: Existing source/modern figure PASS reused by direct authorization, not re-reviewed.
approved_figure_reuse.historical_source_glyph: HOLD; not adjudicated by the permitted modern upright Latin m alias.

clarifications: Initially charged capacitor and zero initial current; no initial magnetic energy. No external energy input; complete damping converts initial stored energy to circuit heat.
exercises.rounding: 5.0e-3 J (5.0 mJ); do not confuse microfarads with millifarads.

clarifications: Ideal initial vacuum/air approximation, circular parallel plates, fringe fields and circuit losses neglected. The source dielectric constant 4 is relative permittivity, not 4 F/m. Full dielectric filling, unchanged geometry and L.
exercises.derivation: A = pi r^2; C0 = epsilon0 A/d; T0 = 2 pi sqrt(L C0); C_filled = 4 C0; T_filled = sqrt(4) T0.
exercises.rounding: Approximately 1.26 microseconds and 2.52 microseconds; the filled period is exactly twice the initial period in this model.

clarifications: Ideal LC frequency relation; C fixed.
exercises.derivation: L(f) = 1/[(2 pi f)^2 C]. Raising f from 400 to 500 Hz lowers L.
exercises.rounding: L spans approximately 10.1 to 15.8 mH; the tuning direction is 15.8 down to 10.1 mH.

clarifications: Single loop, uniform rotation in the standard orientation with rotation axis perpendicular to B so flux spans plus/minus BA. This is an explicit ideal-model clarification, not new numerical data or a new requested part.
exercises.derivation: omega = 2 pi f = 100 pi rad/s; E_m = B A omega = 0.2*pi V.
exercises.rounding: Approximately 0.63 V; the angular factor 2 pi must not be omitted.

clarifications: Frame plane initially perpendicular to B, hence initial flux magnitude is maximum and initial emf is zero. No source-defined terminal polarity or direction; a signed answer requires an explicit convention. Modern E_m is only an amplitude-subscript alias.
exercises.derivation: E_m = n B A omega gives omega = 14/3 rad/s. Choose initial signed flux n B A cos(omega t), then E(t) = -dPhi/dt = E_m sin(omega t). At t=0.1 s, omega t = 7/15 rad.
exercises.rounding: Approximately 0.63 V in magnitude; opposite reference polarity yields -0.63 V. A cosine emf at zero phase is inconsistent with initial maximum flux.

clarifications: Ideal pure inductance; winding resistance neglected; sinusoidal steady-state voltage.
exercises.derivation: X_L = 2 pi f L; I_rms = U_rms/X_L; I_m = sqrt(2) I_rms.
exercises.rounding: Requested amplitude approximately 2.81 A (2.8 A to two significant figures), not 1.99 A rms.

clarifications: Series LC, resistance negligible; impedance magnitude distinguished from complex impedance.
exercises.derivation: X_L = 2 pi f L; X_C = 1/(2 pi f C); complex Z = j(X_L-X_C); |Z| = |X_L-X_C|.
exercises.rounding: Approximately 155 ohms; complex impedance j155 ohms, not a sum of reactance magnitudes.

clarifications: Power means cycle-average real power; voltage and current are sinusoidal and specified as amplitudes. Data determine phase magnitude only, not whether current leads or lags.
exercises.derivation: P = U_rms I_rms cos(phi) = (U_m I_m/2) cos(phi); cos(phi)=0.8; principal phase magnitude arccos(0.8).
exercises.rounding: Approximately 36.9 degrees (0.644 rad); do not use amplitude product as rms product or assert inductive lag.

clarifications: DC means the steady state after the switching transient. AC sinusoidal steady state uses a constant 2 H inductance, series winding resistance, and neglected additional core loss/nonlinearity. The source iron core is retained; this is its textbook linear model, not a replacement with an air-core coil.
exercises.derivation: I_dc=U_dc/R. For AC, X_L=2 pi f L and |Z|=sqrt(R^2+X_L^2), so I_ac,rms=U_ac,rms/|Z|. Peak is optional explanatory conversion, not a new demanded problem part.
exercises.rounding: DC 0.20 A and AC rms approximately 3.98 mA; optional AC peak approximately 5.63 mA.

inputs.circuit: Actual approved Figure 43 inventory: one R, one C, one four-lobed L in a single series path across two source terminals.

clarifications: Sinusoidal steady-state series resonance. Do not remove the actual series resistor or invent a parallel branch. Drawing reference axes and polarity are chosen for the solution; none is attributed to the source.
exercises.derivation: Choose the common current phasor I to the right. V_R=R I is rightward/in phase; V_L=j omega L I is upward; V_C=-j I/(omega C) is downward. At omega L=1/(omega C), |V_L|=|V_C|, so these two opposing voltage phasors cancel. The source phasor V=V_R+V_L+V_C=V_R is rightward and in phase with I; Z=R.

result.source_voltage: equals V_R, in phase with I

clarifications: C2 is parallel to C1, so total capacitance is C1+C2; L unchanged, circuit resistance negligible.
exercises.rounding: 15 microfarads, not 16 microfarads and not a series-capacitance calculation.
